The distributed-line compiler is specified in
[RLGC, Q2D, and Pi Expansion](rlgc-q2d-and-pi-expansion.qmd); the immutable
PTC/transform/retain path and selected-network evidence are specified in

This page keeps their shared physical-graph and logical-Port boundary aligned.

## Compile one backend-neutral physical graph

After ParameterSet binding, the Python compiler expands every component into
oriented physical rows and one ordered node-flux basis. The compile product
carries component, parameter, node, ground, Port, coupling and source provenance.
It forms reciprocal C/K/G evidence for Direct; the compiler does not become the
Plan authority.

The primitive slice follows the canonical
[branch-stamping rule](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/quantum-circuits/physical-circuit-coordinates-node-flux-basis.qmd#g2--stamp-branches-before-interpreting-matrix-entries).
Non-reference node rows use ascending canonical `node_id`; ground has no row.
Components use ascending `component_id`, and rows within one component use its
factory-schema order. For a branch oriented `terminal_1 -> terminal_2`, its
incidence vector $b$ has `+1` at the first non-ground endpoint and `-1` at the
second. A grounded endpoint is simply omitted, so a ground-to-node branch keeps
the sign implied by that same orientation.

The three primitive stamps are

$$
\Delta C=C_b\,\mathbf b\mathbf b^T,
\qquad
\Delta K=L_b^{-1}\mathbf b\mathbf b^T,
\qquad
\Delta G=R_b^{-1}\mathbf b\mathbf b^T.
$$

Every physical value is finite and strictly positive before stamping. The
compiler accumulates complete symmetric Float64 matrices in that basis; it
does not infer orientation from matrix position.

Logical Ports are absent from these intrinsic primitive C/K/G stamps. Direct
selected-network construction subsequently adds the declared Port through its
selector $B$, reference admittance $Y_0$, and source/load boundary, and then
performs the documented de-embedding. This prevents the Port reference
impedance from becoming a DUT resistor.

`run.explain()` uses this compile product to show deterministic rows and maps
without solving. In the Lessons 1–8 slice its presentation contains only the
supported evidence: Plan/request/runtime identity and bound parameters;
Composite hierarchy and public maps; ordered nodes and expanded leaf rows;
C/K/G; Port `B`, `Y0`, load and selected-network
steps; Ref lineage and retained/eliminated coordinates; Direct grid or root
preflight; and, for optimization, variables, unit maps, objectives, expanded
scales, budget, seed, and algorithm IDs. It omits unsupported RLGC,
PTC/transform, N-port, and HB sections instead of printing fabricated `N/A`
rows.

A caller-declared schematic projects the authored Plan through actual body,
pin and wire correspondence. Historical compiled exports projected this
expanded graph; automatic compiled drawing is retired, while the numerical
expansion remains maintained.

## Lower one logical Port

Direct maps each Port to selector column `B`, reference admittance `Y0`, load
stamp `B Y0 B^T`, and power-wave conversion. Selected-network evidence retains
the node, orientation, reference impedance and actual load boundary.

PTC removes only declared, evidenced `nonloading_probe` loads from the analysis
network.
Its canonical port set, transform ordering, retained-coordinate order, and
selected-network maps are fixed in
[View Lineage and Selected Networks](view-lineage-and-selected-networks.qmd).

## Replay one ordered view lineage

The compiler replays the public order—bound graph, optional PTC, ordered paired
transforms, optional terminal retain, then zero-current complement elimination.
The exact lineage grammar, ParameterSet-dependent weights, port
canonicalization, N-port realizability, and failure evidence live in
[View Lineage and Selected Networks](view-lineage-and-selected-networks.qmd).
Direct quantities may evaluate a named unported coordinate; Direct S/Y/Z matrix
requests require a Port-realizable final basis and fail rather than returning a smaller or
backend-specific fallback view.
